title: Technical Leadership
description: Mentoring and delegating through inspectable artifacts, influencing without relying on hire-and-fire authority, and making technical decisions that other people and teams have to live with.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can produce a written 1:1 agenda, a delegation brief, or a review note that names a specific deliverable or observed behavior (not a personality trait) and a next check-in date.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can complete a scoped mentoring or delegation cycle and leave inspectable artifacts: an agenda used in a real or role-played 1:1, review comments labeled blocking versus advisory, and a follow-up that records an owner and a date for each action.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently write a team-scope technical decision (ADR or equivalent brief) that names at least two rejected alternatives, states who outside the author's team is affected, and records at least one accepted negative consequence.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can produce a cross-team influence brief that anticipates named objections from another team, states what the author will give up, and revises the ask after a stated counter-argument without collapsing into 'do both.'

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can write and defend a 90-day team technical strategy that names what the team will stop doing, how each bet is owned, and which bet would be cut if a named constraint changed — and can walk another lead through producing the same class of artifact.
